findings.what: The regex that strips the closing instruction stops at any full stop, so it misses "Slide the damping down to 0.02 and the peak climbs to 1.5 mm." because of the decimal points; the read-through keeps the instruction to slide and then repeats "At 0.02 the peak climbs to 1.5 mm." (RUNBOOK 6b).

findings.where: Screen 4 (The critical speed) and puzzle 13 (Stiffer mounts)
findings.what: Screen 4 gives "15.9 times a second" without its rule; no screen before puzzle 13 shows natural frequency = √(stiffness ÷ mass) = √(500,000 ÷ 50) = 100 rad/s, but puzzle 13 and its hint depend on it. Add that line to screen 4 and trim elsewhere, since it is already at 89 words.

0.06 mm (where the shake settles, and the base of the peak rule) is never worked out where Dan can see it, though it is m r ÷ M = 0.003 ÷ 50 m. The peak rule 0.06 mm ÷ (2 × the damping factor) is stated without its reason: at the critical speed the spring and the rotor's inertia cancel, so only damping holds back the pull. Both are skipped steps, and the number does not come from a rule on screen.

The promised condition monitoring is missing: vibration reveals unbalance, misalignment, looseness, worn bearings and gear wear; misalignment is the commonest cause after unbalance; spectrum analysis tells the causes apart; ISO 20816-1 is named once. Only a one-line alignment tip survives in practice.

findings.where: Screen 14 (What builds on this) and explain paragraph 3
findings.what: "Two ideas build on this one" is wrong, because bending and twist build on moments and stress, not on vibration. The screen never says these come in his Level 3 course next year, and never names Heat and fluids as the next course. "Good balance lets it carry that torque smoothly" is a vague claim nothing supports, and the same gearbox sentences sit as a non sequitur before the explain's closing summary.

findings.where: Screen 14 sketch, the two torque arcs
findings.what: The torque arrows are circular arcs in the page plane, clockwise at the left end and anticlockwise at the right. That is the symbol for a bending couple that would sag the bar, not for a twist about the shaft's own axis. Draw each torque as an arc wrapping round the shaft, with opposite senses at the two ends.

The lesson carries seven footnote markers ([^2], [^3] twice, [^4], [^5], [^6], [^1]), most on plain ideas he would never look up ("the pull is four times as big", "a lower, wider peak") and one on the bold summary sentence. The rule allows a few, on values he would look up; keep the 10% margin and drop most of the others.

The 300 to 1450 rev/min glide passes the critical speed, so the shake readout spikes to about 0.58 mm and falls again before resonance has been introduced. No word explains it. Meanwhile the mounts' up-and-down movement the text promises is about one drawing unit at 1450 rev/min, so it cannot be seen.

findings.where: Rotor screens, shake bracket beside the beam
findings.what: The bracket labelled "shake" spans the full travel, from −A to +A, while the readout "Shake at the mounts" gives the amplitude A. Say which one the number is, because on the job vibration displacement is often quoted peak to peak.

About 130 px of blank space sits between the spring sketch and the answer buttons, held for working lines. The opening screen is also completely still; the mass could bob slowly at its own 2 Hz so it looks alive.

findings.where: Caption under the figure, every screen
findings.what: "An example rotor, turning 20 times slower than real, with its shake drawn 40 times bigger" shows on screen 1's spring, on the puzzles with no rotor and on screen 14. Show it only on the rotor screens.
The lead sits above the progress bar and shows only on screen 2, so the bar and the step label jump down and back up between screens 1, 2 and 3.
Play again only replays the fade-in of two still sketches, so the button does nothing useful there.

findings.where: Puzzle 9 (Balance mass), Why? and working lines
findings.what: "30 × 0.10 = 3" has no unit, and the working mixes grams and metres; write 3 g m.
The damping factor is never given a meaning. One line recalling that 1 is critical damping (Differential equations lesson 6) would show Dan that 0.05 is light damping.

findings.where: Screen 6 line under the picture, after a manual move
findings.what: In "... = 0.06 ÷ (2 × 0.20) = 0.150 mm. At 955 rev/min it is 0.150 mm." the 0.06 has no unit. At the critical speed the second sentence also just repeats the first.
"Doubling the damping halves it. So avoid a running speed near a critical speed." The "So" does not follow from the damping sentence; move that advice to after the peak.
The brief's "heavier goes slower" is never shown; only stiffer mounts are tried. The "more than one critical speed" line could name normal modes from Linear algebra lesson 7, as the brief asks.

The only margin given is for twisting vibration, which is honest to the source, but the lesson teaches side-to-side critical speeds. Say in one sentence that the lesson gives no fixed margin for that case.
